- Real-time interactive gameplay (falling tetrominoes, player movement/rotation)

- Keyboard input handling
- Dynamic scoring and game state management
- Progressive difficulty (increasing drop speed)

**Modality Evaluation:**
- **Image/Document/PowerPoint/Excel/PDF/Mind Map**: These are static or presentation-oriented formats — completely unsuitable for an interactive game.
- **Dashboard**: Designed for real-time information display, not for interactive gameplay with user input.
- **Website**: Could technically work via HTML/JavaScript, but may have limitations with keyboard responsiveness and game loop performance in some environments.
- **Application**: A Python-based application (e.g., using pygame or tkinter) is ideal — it natively supports real-time game loops, keyboard event handling, graphical rendering of the board and tetrominoes, and smooth animation for falling pieces and line-clearing effects.

{"verdict": "changes_requested", "issues": [{"file": "main.py", "line": 159, "message": "toggle_pause() schedules a new gravity loop on unpause without cancelling a still-pending after() job. If the player presses P twice quickly (pause then unpause within one tick interval), two loop callbacks are pending; each fires, ticks, and reschedules itself, creating permanent duplicate gravity chains (piece falls at 2x+ speed, worsening with every rapid pause/unpause). reset() only cancels the latest self.job id, so ghost loops also survive a restart. Fix: in toggle_pause(), call root.after_cancel(self.job) (guarding for a stale/already-fired id, which is a safe no-op) before scheduling on unpause, and cancel the pending job when pausing, so exactly one loop chain exists at all times."}]}
